# yolo-twice

**Transparent agentic development superpowers.** See what your coding agent did, at the
zoom level you choose, while it is still running.

## The problem

A long Claude Code session leaves behind megabytes of JSONL: hundreds of turns, tool calls,
subagent transcripts, rewinds and compactions. Reading it as a chat list does not scale, and
the existing viewers, good as they are, show exactly that list. You either micro-manage every
tool call or you go full yolo and lose track of what happened.

## What yolo-twice does

- **Semantic zoom.** Read a session as one line, three sentences, a paragraph of phases, the
  turns, or the raw records. Any text, including the top summary and a long tool result, can be
  zoomed out one more step or expanded in place.
- **Live flow graph.** The conversation as a graph: turns, tool calls, subagents and rewind
  branches, updated while the session runs, merging into phases as you zoom out.
- **Attention slider.** From "micro management" (every turn summarized live) to "yolo"
  (nothing until you ask, then "catch me up"). You choose how many tokens and how much
  attention to spend; the cost is shown next to the slider.
- **Linked views, shareable links.** Filter bar, timeline, reader and graph react to each
  other: drag a time window, click to zoom into a phase or turn, filter to your prompts
  or tool errors, and every view follows. The URL captures the whole view, so a link opens
  exactly what you saw.
- **Project-local history.** Everything derived lands in `.yolo-twice/` in your repo,
  redacted, plain JSON and mermaid, so you can commit it or gitignore it.
- **Incremental and idempotent.** Stop the engine, resume later, run it twice: same bytes.

## Install

One command, in a terminal where Claude Code is installed (version 2.1.275 or newer, Node 22
or newer):

```
claude plugin install yolo-twice --marketplace bar9/yolo-twice
```

## Use

Inside any Claude Code session (plugin commands are namespaced, so the command is `/yolo-twice:yolo-twice`):

```
/yolo-twice:yolo-twice                  start the engine for this project and open the UI
/yolo-twice:yolo-twice stop             stop the engine
/yolo-twice:yolo-twice status           show engine, session and index state
/yolo-twice:yolo-twice mode yolo        set the attention slider: micro | attentive | balanced | yolo
/yolo-twice:yolo-twice resume [id]      rebuild a committed session's transcript and print the claude --resume command
```

New to the UI? Help (the ? button in the header) has a short guide and a one-minute guided tour.
Press `?` for the keyboard shortcuts: ← → move between levels, ↑ ↓ through parts, − + change the
detail, `/` searches.

The same commands work from a terminal via the engine CLI, for example `yolo-twice status` or
`yolo-twice index` for a one-shot index without the daemon.

# Plan for issue #2: show authors

## What the code has today
- **No author anywhere.** Claude Code's JSONL doesn't record one, our `Event` schema doesn't ([schema.ts:33](packages/core/src/schema.ts#L33)), and neither does `SessionMeta` ([store.ts:16](packages/core/src/store.ts#L16)).
- So the author has to be **the person whose engine first ingested the session**. Only that machine has the source JSONL.
- **Resume makes a new session.** `prepareResume` uses `--fork-session` ([resume.ts:181](packages/engine/src/resume.ts#L181)), so the continuation gets a new session id. That new session opens with the original author's history, and then a second person takes over. This is the one place the author changes *inside* a session.
- **One trap:** `deriveSession` rewrites `meta.json` from scratch on every rebuild ([pipeline.ts:15](packages/analyzers/src/pipeline.ts#L15)). A naive fix would let a teammate's engine overwrite the author with their own name.

## Design

**1. Data: record the author once per session, in `meta.json` (committed)**
```json
"author": { "name": "Matthias Cullmann", "email_sha256": "…" }
```
- **Source:** `git config user.name` / `user.email` in the project root. If those aren't set, leave `author` out (don't fall back to the OS login, since redaction turns that into `<user>`).
- **Store a SHA-256 of the email, not the email.** That's enough for Gravatar, and it keeps the committed folder close to its "redacted" promise.
- **Write it once, then never change it.** `deriveSession` copies `author` over from the existing meta. This keeps the "run it twice, same bytes" rule.
- **Backfill:** older sessions without an author get the first committer of their `meta.json` from `git log --diff-filter=A`. That's literally a git blame.
- Pass `author` through to `ProjectIndex.sessions[]` so the UI gets it for free.

**2. Forks: show where the author changes**
- Add `"forked_from": { "session": "<id>", "until": "<event id>" }` to the forked session's meta. Events up to `until` belong to the original session's author.
- **Spike first (about 30 min):** check what `claude --resume <file> --fork-session` writes. If it keeps our record `uuid`s (or our `version: "yolo-twice"` marker), we match on those. If not, we match the first prompt's text and timestamp against committed sessions on first ingest of a new session.

**3. UI: show the author only where it changes**
- **Session table** ([App.tsx:910](packages/ui/src/App.tsx#L910)): an avatar in the title cell, shown only on the first row of a run of sessions by the same person. Otherwise it's just faint on hover.
- **Hover card / tooltip, git-blame style:** "by Matthias · resumed from Bar's session 34b27ceb" in `HoverCard` ([App.tsx:841](packages/ui/src/App.tsx#L841)).
- **Reader (Zoom):** a single "↪ Matthias takes over" divider at the fork point, nothing on each message.
- **Graph:** a small avatar on session nodes at the project level only.
- **Later:** an author filter in the FilterBar.

**4. Toggle: off by default for solo repos**
- `authors.show: "auto" | "on" | "off"` in `config.json` sets the team default. Personal overrides go in `local.json`, the same pattern as `attention` ([project.ts:141](packages/engine/src/project.ts#L141)).
- **`auto` (the default)** shows authors only when the project has more than one distinct author. A repo with one developer never sees them, and no one has to configure anything.
- Add a toggle in the Header settings, backed by `GET`/`PUT /api/config`.

**5. Avatars**
- Use `https://gravatar.com/avatar/<sha256>?s=64&d=404`. If that fails, show initials on a colour derived from the hash. Initials also cover offline, Docker and people without a Gravatar.
- `authors.avatars: "gravatar" | "initials"`. Loading Gravatar sends a request to an outside service, so a team can switch it off.

## Work items
| # | Task | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add `author` and `forked_from` to `SessionMeta`/`ProjectIndex`, keep `author` on rewrite, add `authors` to the config schema | core `schema.ts`, `store.ts`, analyzers `pipeline.ts` |
| 2 | Read the author from git at first ingest, plus the git-log backfill | engine `project.ts` (new `author.ts`) |
| 3 | Fork spike, then fork detection on first ingest | engine `resume.ts`, core `ingest.ts` |
| 4 | `<Avatar>` component (Gravatar, falling back to initials), session table, hover card | ui `App.tsx`, new `Avatar.tsx` |
| 5 | "Takes over" divider in the reader, avatars on project-level graph nodes | ui `Zoom.tsx`, `Graph.tsx` |
| 6 | `auto`/`on`/`off` setting, saved locally, plus the Header toggle | engine `server.ts`, ui `Header.tsx`, `api.ts` |
| 7 | Tests: author kept across rebuilds, idempotent bytes, `auto` with one vs two authors, fork matching | core/engine tests |

**Suggested cut for today:** items 1, 2, 4 and 6 give you faces on sessions with no noise in solo repos. Items 3 and 5 (fork takeover) depend on the spike.

**Decision for you:** is a SHA-256 of the email in committed `meta.json` acceptable, or should Gravatar be opt-in only, with no hash stored unless it's switched on?

Teams share sessions through the committed `.yolo-twice/` folder and continue a teammate's session with `resume`. The display can be switched on or off per repo and per user, so repos with one developer see no extra noise, and people show up with an avatar.

## Approach

### 1. Data: record the author once per session in `meta.json` (committed)
- `author: { name, email_sha256 }`, taken from `git config user.name/user.email` in the project root when the session is first ingested. If those aren't set, leave `author` out (don't use the OS login, since redaction turns it into `<user>`).
- Store a SHA-256 of the email, not the email. That's enough for Gravatar.
- **Write once, never change.** `deriveSession` ([pipeline.ts:15](packages/analyzers/src/pipeline.ts#L15)) rewrites meta on every rebuild, so it must copy `author` (and `forked_from`) over from the existing meta. That stops a teammate's engine from writing its own name over the author, and keeps output byte-identical.
- Backfill for older sessions: use the first committer of `sessions/<id>/meta.json` via `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%an%x00%ae`. Reuse the `execFile("git", …)` helper pattern from [autocommit.ts](packages/engine/src/autocommit.ts).
- Pass `author` through to `ProjectIndex.sessions[]` (`buildProjectIndex`, [store.ts](packages/core/src/store.ts)).

### 2. Forks: the point where the author changes inside a session
- `prepareResume` uses `--fork-session` ([resume.ts](packages/engine/src/resume.ts)), so the resumed session gets a new id and opens with the original author's history.
- Add `forked_from: { session, until }` to the new session's meta. Events up to `until` belong to the original session's author.
- **Spike first:** check whether a forked JSONL keeps our record `uuid`s or the `version: "yolo-twice"` marker. If it does, match on those. If not, match the first prompt's text and timestamp against committed sessions when a new session is first ingested.

### 3. UI: show the author only where it changes
- New `Avatar.tsx`: `https://gravatar.com/avatar/<sha256>?s=64&d=404`. If that fails, show initials on a colour derived from the hash.
- Session table ([App.tsx ~910](packages/ui/src/App.tsx)): avatar plus name only on the first row of a run of sessions by the same author.
- `HoverCard` ([App.tsx ~841](packages/ui/src/App.tsx)): a git-blame style line, "by X · resumed from Y's session abcd1234".
- Reader ([Zoom.tsx](packages/ui/src/Zoom.tsx)): a single "X takes over" divider at the fork point.
- Graph ([Graph.tsx](packages/ui/src/Graph.tsx)): avatars on session nodes at the project level only.

### 4. Settings
- Add `authors: { show: "auto"|"on"|"off", avatars: "gravatar"|"initials" }` to the `Config` schema. `config.json` holds the team default, and `local.json` (`LocalConfig`, [store.ts:27](packages/core/src/store.ts#L27)) holds personal overrides, the same pattern as `attention` ([project.ts:141](packages/engine/src/project.ts#L141)).
- `auto` (the default) shows authors only when the project has more than one distinct author.
- Add a toggle in [Header.tsx](packages/ui/src/Header.tsx) through the existing `GET`/`PUT /api/config` ([server.ts:278](packages/engine/src/server.ts#L278)).

## Order
1. Schema, keeping `author` on rewrite, config (core, analyzers)
2. Reading the author from git and the backfill (engine, new `author.ts`)
3. Avatar, session table, hover card, settings toggle (ui)
4. Fork spike, then `forked_from`, the "takes over" divider, graph avatars

## Verification
- Unit tests: `author` survives `deriveSession` and the bytes are identical; the backfill reads git log in a temp repo; `auto` hides authors with one author and shows them with two; fork matching on the fixture.
- `bun test` across the packages.
- Manual: run the engine on this repo, use `/run` and the browser to check the session table and hover card, then add a second author by hand in another meta and confirm the avatars appear. Toggle the setting off and confirm they disappear.

Is a SHA-256 of the email in committed `meta.json` acceptable, or should storing it be opt-in?

{"plan":"# Show authors (issue #2)

## Context
Teams share sessions through the committed `.yolo-twice/` folder and continue each other's sessions with `resume`. Nothing in the UI says who wrote what. The goal is to show the author where it changes, git-blame style, with a face (Gravatar). We add **no new stored data and no setting**:
- **Authors come from git.** Every line of `sessions/<id>/events.ndjson` was committed by the engine of the person who ingested it, so `git blame` on that file gives the author of each event.
- **We show authors only where they change**, so a solo repo shows nothing, and a toggle isn't needed.

## Approach

### 1. Engine: blame the events file (new `packages/engine/src/authors.ts`)
- `git blame --line-porcelain -- .yolo-twice/sessions/<id>/events.ndjson`, run with the `execFile("git", …)` pattern from [autocommit.ts](packages/engine/src/autocommit.ts).
- Map each line to its event `id` (parse the JSON line) and its `author` / `author-mail`. Collapse consecutive lines by the same author into runs: `{ first, last, name, email_sha256 }`. The email is hashed on the server, so the raw address never reaches the UI.
- Lines that aren't committed yet (blame's `Not Committed Yet`) belong to the local `git config user.name/email`, marked `uncommitted: true`.
- Not a git repo, or the file isn't tracked: return `[]`, and the UI shows nothing.
- Cache the result in `cache/authors/<id>.json`, keyed on `git rev-parse HEAD` plus the events file size. Autocommit moves HEAD, which refreshes it.
- Project level: each session's author set (distinct names in its runs) goes into `/api/sessions` so the session table and graph get it without extra calls.

### 2. API
- `GET /api/sessions/:id/authors` returns the runs. Register it next to the other session routes in [server.ts](packages/engine/src/server.ts) (~line 182), behind the existing `checkId`.
- Add `authors?: {name, email_sha256}[]` to each entry of the `/api/sessions` response (computed in the engine, not written to `meta.json`).

### 3. Forks / resume
- `--fork-session` ([resume.ts](packages/engine/src/resume.ts)) writes a new session, and its file starts with a copy of the original history. Blame would credit that copy to the person who resumed.
- **Spike first:** check whether the forked JSONL keeps the original record uuids, and with them our event ids. If it does, any event whose id also appears in another committed session takes that session's blame author. That's a few lines in `authors.ts`. If it doesn't, accept the misattribution for now and note it in the issue.

### 4. UI: show the author only where it changes
- New `Avatar.tsx`: `https://gravatar.com/avatar/<sha256>?s=64&d=404`. If that fails, show initials on a colour derived from the hash.
- Rule: render nothing unless the project has more than one distinct author. When it does, show an avatar on the first item of each run.

Run from the Claude Code VS Code extension, that's an awkward detour. When we're inside the extension, the fork should open directly in a new Claude tab in VS Code.

What we found:
- **Detection:** the extension starts Claude with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=claude-vscode`. Plugin command shell lines inherit it.
- **Opening a tab:** the extension (`anthropic.claude-code`) registers a URI handler. `vscode://anthropic.claude-code/open?session=<id>[&prompt=…]` runs `claude-vscode.primaryEditor.open(session, prompt)`, which opens that session in an editor tab.
- **Catch:** the handler takes a session *id*, not a file path. Claude finds sessions by id in `~/.claude/projects/<project slug>/<id>.jsonl`. Today's resume only writes to `.yolo-twice/cache/resume/` and lets `--fork-session` create the new id.

## Approach

### 1. Spike (5 min)
Write a rebuilt transcript to `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<new uuid>.jsonl`, with every `sessionId` set to the new uuid. Then run `code --open-url "vscode://anthropic.claude-code/open?session=<uuid>"`. Confirm the tab opens with the history and that a new prompt continues it. If the extension refuses the session, stop and fall back to printing the command.

### 2. Engine: fork into Claude's project folder (`packages/engine/src/resume.ts`)
- New `prepareFork(store, root, session?)`: reuse `reconstructTranscript`, pick `crypto.randomUUID()` as the new id, and write the lines with `sessionId` set to that id. Write to `claudeProjectDir(root)` (core, already used by `ProjectRuntime`) as `<uuid>.jsonl`, mode 0600.
- Doing the fork ourselves keeps today's guarantee: the committed session never gets a second writer.
- Update the header comment, since "Nothing is written to ~/.claude" no longer holds for this path.
- The engine's watcher on that folder ingests the new session, just as it ingests a `--fork-session` today.

### 3. CLI: open the tab when in VS Code (`packages/engine/src/cli.ts`, `case "resume"`)
- If `process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT === "claude-vscode"`: run `prepareFork`, then open `vscode://anthropic.claude-code/open?session=<uuid>` with `code --open-url <uri>`. If `code` isn't on `PATH`, fall back to the platform opener (`xdg-open` / `open` / `cmd /c start`).
  - Print `opened a fork of session <id8> in a new VS Code tab (<uuid8>)`.
  - If opening fails, print today's terminal command as a fallback.
- Otherwise: no change (terminal command, or spawn `claude` on a TTY).
- `--print` keeps forcing the terminal command.

### 4. Plugin command text (`code/plugin/commands/twice.md`)
Relay line: "If it says a VS Code tab was opened, say so in one line."
